deployment::the public resolver runs a t.what: the public resolver runs a third codebase
deployment::the public resolver runs a t.why: moltrust-uresolver.service runs node server.js from ~/driver-did-moltrust, a repository that never published an image, while the published image comes from uni-resolver-driver-did-moltrust/index.js. The two answer differently for a malformed identifier: the deployed service says notFound, the published 1.0.0 image said internalError, and 1.1.0 says invalidDid. The fix shipped in 1.1.0 is in neither running thing.

derivation::identifiers are not derived.what: identifiers are not derived from the key
derivation::identifiers are not derived.why: Section 2.2 requires the method-specific identifier to be the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the agent's Ed25519 public key. All seven places that mint a DID use uuid.uuid4().hex[:16], so the shape conforms and the derivation does not. This affects every one of the 532 registered DIDs, and /identity/register-pop has the public key in hand and still does not use it.

ext_::DID_PATTERN accepts a prefix the s.what: DID_PATTERN accepts a prefix the specification does not define
ext_::DID_PATTERN accepts a prefix the s.why: DID_PATTERN allows did:moltrust:ext_ plus 16 hex. Section 2.2 defines no prefix and section 6 describes the bridge without one. One row uses it, did:moltrust:ext_516a656bafa39e5c, while 18 of the 19 rows in did_bridges map to a conformant identifier. Open decision: the prefix leaves the pattern, or it enters the specification.

keys-symmetry::kid in did.json without a.what: kid in did.json without a JWK: did:web:api.moltrust.ch#key-ed25519
keys-symmetry::kid in did.json without a.why: did.json names this verification method for assertionMethod and authentication, and jwks.json publishes no key under that kid, so a verifier that follows the DID document cannot obtain the key it is told to use.

keys-symmetry::kid in jwks.json without.what: kid in jwks.json without a verification method: did:web:moltrust.ch#moltguard-key-1
keys-symmetry::kid in jwks.json without.why: This kid belongs to did:web:moltrust.ch, a different subject from did:web:api.moltrust.ch whose document is served here, so it could not appear in that document at all; it is published from the wrong place.

keys-symmetry::kid in jwks.json without.what: kid in jwks.json without a verification method: moltrust-gateway-v1
keys-symmetry::kid in jwks.json without.why: jwks.json publishes this as use=sig while the DID document does not declare it, so a signature made with it is unverifiable for anyone who starts from the DID document.

keys-symmetry::kid in jwks.json without.what: kid in jwks.json without a verification method: moltrust-registry-2026-v1
keys-symmetry::kid in jwks.json without.why: Same shape as moltrust-gateway-v1: published as a signing key, absent from the DID document.

spec::section 6 omits the X-API-Key the.what: section 6 omits the X-API-Key the endpoint requires
spec::section 6 omits the X-API-Key the.why: Section 6 shows POST /identity/bridge-simple with Content-Type only, while the endpoint requires X-API-Key and answers 401 without it. Sections 4.1, 4.3 and 4.4 do show the header, so the omission is in section 6 alone.

spec::the DID document does not carry de.what: the DID document does not carry deactivated
spec::the DID document does not carry de.where: _build_did_document in app/main.py, section 4.4 of the specification
spec::the DID document does not carry de.why: Section 4.4 states that on deactivation the DID document is marked deactivated: true. The document of a revoked agent carries no such member; revocation lives in agents.revoked_at and surfaces through /identity/verify, so a W3C resolver sees a revoked agent as a valid one. Checked live against did:moltrust:347a460acae84446, revoked 2026-09-20.

urls-resolve::URL named publicly answers.where: app/main.py:7346 in moltrust-api, section 4.4 of the method specification
urls-resolve::URL named publicly answers.why: Section 4.4 documents the path without the DID segment and the DID in the body; the route is POST /identity/revoke/{did} with the DID in the path, so the capability exists and the documented address does not.

Section 4.3 describes key rotation, a revoked marker on the old key and a revokedDate in the DID document; none of it exists — no route in app/, nothing in the OpenAPI document, and the DID document carries one key.
